solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Row of houses whose rafters so rickety

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters of these words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A terrace of homes whose roof timbers are shaky and unsound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line of buildings and 'houses' like homes, but the row is a quarrel and the houses are the royal houses of York and Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century civil wars were a dynastic conflict (a row) between two royal families, the houses of York and Lancaster.

clue.text: Rising tide has Midwest state within range

indicators.note: within says the state's abbreviation goes inside the other piece
in a down clue, rising means the word for tide is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the tide is the sea
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota, a Midwestern US state

explanation.surface: A flood tide surges into a mountain range somewhere in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads the tide word upwards, as down clues allow; 'within' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain range running down the western side of South America.

clue.text: Wakes around middle of day for flight

indicators.note: around says the first piece is wrapped about the next one

parts.note: wakes means stirs, as a sleeper does

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Someone rouses at about midday before catching a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a set of steps, not an air journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a run of steps between floors of a building, which is what stairs form.

clue.text: Klutz gets in processed seafood — from him?

definitions.text: Klutz gets in processed seafood — from him?

indicators.note: gets in says the word for a klutz is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a fish finger is a processed seafood product, so the clue gives the second word, finger
a shmo (also schmo) is US slang for a clumsy fool, like a klutz

explanation.surface: A clumsy oaf gets mixed up in fish processing, and the question asks who sold it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' signals the insertion. The whole clue is also the definition: processed seafood might come from a seller of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in fish is the trader from whom you might buy seafood, processed or not.

clue.text: Boundary in park comprising two hectares

indicators.note: two says the abbreviation is written twice in a row

parts.note: HA is the standard abbreviation for hectare

explanation.surface: A parkland boundary encloses an area of two hectares.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch with a wall, used in British country-house parks as a boundary that keeps livestock out without blocking the view.
explanation.definitionFit: This sunken fence is the classic invisible boundary in landscaped English parkland.

clue.text: Stop phoning Beatle, foremost of Fab Four

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the drummer of the Beatles

indicators.note: foremost of picks the leading letter of each of the two words Fab and Four

explanation.surface: A demand to end calls to a Beatle, the leading member of the Fab Four.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fab Four was the nickname of the Beatles, but here the words only supply their first letters, F and F.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a telephone call is to hang up, a phrasal verb meaning to stop the conversation on the line.

clue.text: Has a very bad argument from which expensive suit may come

definitions.text: from which expensive suit may come

parts.note: has can be shortened to 's, as in he's done it
vile means very bad
a row is an argument

explanation.surface: A furious quarrel that might end in a costly lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like a legal action after an argument; it is clothing. Savile Row is a London street famous for bespoke tailors.
explanation.definitionFit: This London street is home to high-end bespoke tailors, so a costly made-to-measure jacket and trousers may come from there.

clue.text: Heroine having a pulse yet being out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heroine who still has a pulse but is unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out' looks like unconsciousness, which fits the fairy tale, but 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The princess cursed to sleep for a hundred years is the title character of a famous fairy tale and ballet.

clue.text: I'm in a rain dance possibly

definitions.text: I'm in a rain dance possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters are one of the possible arrangements, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone says they are taking part in a ceremonial dance to bring rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the speaker who might join a rain dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain dances are associated with Native peoples of North America, so the speaker is one of them.

clue.text: Old Indian city has backed faith school

parts.note: Madras is the former name of Chennai

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word has is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A historic city in India is home to a religious school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like support but turns HAS into SAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrassah is an Islamic religious school, so it is an educational institution grounded in faith.

clue.text: More brilliant lights reflected in European river

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means the letters for European river are read backwards

parts.note: the Avon is a river in England

explanation.surface: Lights shine more brightly where they are mirrored in a river on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns E AVON into NOVA E.
explanation.definitionFit: Novae are stars that suddenly flare up to many times their usual brightness, so they are lights grown more brilliant.

clue.text: Run out to play instrument with strings on stage

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
to strum is to play a guitar or similar by brushing the strings

explanation.surface: A musician rushes off to perform a guitar on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman dismissed by having the wicket broken while running is 'run out', abbreviated RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker or performer, a kind of small stage.

clue.text: Helping attractive girl with work

parts.note: doll is slang for an attractive young woman
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A good-looking girl assists with some work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like assistance; it is a noun, a serving of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless lump of food served out, a portion on the plate.

clue.text: Versatile sportsman allowed to enter cheated appallingly

indicators.note: to enter says the word for allowed goes inside the other piece
appallingly means very badly, so the letters of cheated are scrambled

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: An all-round athlete is permitted to compete after shamelessly cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appallingly' scrambles the fodder to DECATHE, and 'to enter' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlete competes in ten different track and field events, so must be an all-rounder.

clue.text: What's company about? It produces drug

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A question about what a firm does, answered by its drug output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives CA (circa), not a sense of surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: The coca shrub is the plant from whose leaves cocaine is extracted.

clue.text: Shortly show up loose woman, about 50, not actually married

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: to show up is to come

indicators.note: about says the jumbled word goes round the numeral
loose means free and unfixed, so the letters of woman are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A disreputable woman in her fifties appears, though she is not truly a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' drops a final letter; 'loose' scrambles to MONAW, and 'about' wraps that round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A common-law wife or husband lives with a partner as a couple without a formal wedding.

clue.text: Antiviral agent physician's injected iron men sent back

indicators.note: injected says the following pieces are put inside the word for the physician

parts.note: an intern is a junior hospital doctor; the 's stands for has
FE is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: sent back means the word for men is read in reverse

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, the men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A doctor has given iron injections to men who were turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is a military abbreviation for enlisted men; 'sent back' makes it RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Interferon is a protein the body makes that interferes with viruses multiplying.

clue.text: Arrange start of espousal with mate handy

definitions.text: Arrange start of espousal with mate handy

indicators.note: arrange means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged
start of picks the opening letter of espousal

explanation.surface: Fix a wedding date while the partner is present.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: to fix when a marriage begins, with the partner at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to set the date of a wedding, which is arranging when the espousal starts.

clue.text: Call on Hunt to put in partner with hospital

indicators.note: put in says the following pieces go inside the word to

parts.note: an ally is a partner
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone the Hunt family to bring in a partner with a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' looks like a surname but is a fox hunt; 'put in' signals the insertion into the little word 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cry hunters give on sighting the fox, a call heard during a hunt.

clue.text: Perhaps Cornish sailor will get to clean the deck

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, so something Cornish is an example of SW
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor from Cornwall will be told to scrub the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the far south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To swab is to mop a ship's deck with a cloth or mop, a sailor's chore.

clue.text: Bird soaring well above quarry

indicators.note: above says the first piece sits over the next in the down entry
in a down clue, soaring means the word for well is read upwards

parts.note: so means well, as in 'so, what now?'
quarry is a hunted animal, prey

explanation.surface: A bird flies high above the creature it is hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaring' turns SO into OS, placed above PREY.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a large fish-eating bird of prey.

clue.text: Nut's part of vegetarian diet

definitions.meaning: a strip of pasta that can form part of a meat-free meal

explanation.surface: A crank who follows a meat-free regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal for the head, and pasta strands are a staple that vegetarians eat.

clue.text: Noah's upset about an exclamation of praise

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the word an
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Noah is distressed by a shout of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles to HOSNA, and 'about' wraps that round the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a shout of adoration to God, used in Christian and Jewish worship.

clue.text: Engineers snare uprising in African country

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means these letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
a gin is a trap for catching game

explanation.surface: Engineers trap a rebellion in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' looks like a revolt but turns RE GIN upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Kiss old film star

definitions.meaning: a quick light kiss on the cheek
Gregory ..., the Hollywood actor of To Kill a Mockingbird

explanation.surface: A kiss from a vintage screen idol.
explanation.definitionFit: A peck is a brief kiss, and Gregory Peck was a leading Hollywood actor of the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: Chase popular song

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Pursue a hit tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chase' is not pursuit: to chase metal is to engrave or set decoration into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasing is ornamenting metal by engraving or embedding, close to setting decoration into a surface.

clue.text: Order given to marchers certainly leads to support for drill in the back

indicators.note: in says the following pieces go inside the reversed word
back means the word the is read in reverse

parts.note: yes means certainly; leads to just says it comes first
a rig is a framework supporting an oil drill

explanation.surface: A command to soldiers on parade, involving support for drilling in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals reading the backwards, and 'in' puts the rest inside. 'drill' looks like parade practice but is an oil drill.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a parade-ground command telling marching soldiers to turn their heads to the right.

clue.text: A standard worry — wonky knee cracking up

indicators.note: cracking up means falling apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An ordinary concern about a dodgy knee that is breaking down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A standard' looks like a level or norm, but is a much-performed popular song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kander and Ebb song made famous by Sinatra is a classic of the popular repertoire.
